_comment: WHY THIS GATE NEEDS A COMMITTED CASE (ADR 0008): it is a gate that lets
work THROUGH - ADR 0008 row 31, a prerequisite of `make verify`, whose
green is read by sessions and by other repos as 'the vendored engine is
the one upstream published'. Nothing downstream re-derives it. A blind
version prints the same '16 files match' line over a drifted tree.
WHY IT COULD NOT BE REGISTERED BEFORE #1012: VENDOR_ROOT and
MANIFEST_PATH were module-level constants, so the gate could only ever
read THIS repository and could not be aimed at a known-bad tree.
`--root` is what made a committed case possible.
THE CASES CARRY ALL 16 CONTRACT PATHS, and must: the manifest file set is
checked against the hardcoded vendoring contract BEFORE any hash is
compared, so a case with fewer paths is refused for the wrong reason and
never reaches the comparison under test. Their CONTENT is a placeholder
of a few bytes each - the question is whether the gate can tell matching
bytes from drifted bytes, not whether it can host 176K of real engine
Stdlib-only, network-free and git-free, like the gate.
detect_signal: ^DRIFT: .* does not match the manifest pin\.$
limits: Covers the OFFLINE per-file hash comparison. It says nothing about whether the REAL vendored tree is correct - that is the gate's own run under `make verify`, over the real tree - and nothing about the advisory `--upstream` half (ADR 0008 row 32), which needs a network. The manifest-validation and contract-version paths are exercised by tests/test_project_next_vendor.py rather than by a committed case, because each needs a differently-malformed manifest and a case can only carry one.

cases.name: bad-drifted-file
cases.why: One line appended to lib/project_next/models.py with its pin untouched - a local edit to the vendored engine instead of a fix upstream in codex-power-pack. Per-file pins exist so a failure names the exact file; if this scores GOOD they name nothing.

cases.name: good-pinned-files
cases.why: The same 16-file tree with every file matching its pin. Separates a working gate from one wedged at 'fail', which the bad case alone cannot do - and this gate is a prerequisite of `make verify`, so a wedged one blocks every merge.

anchors.why: CONSTRUCTED, not historical: the pre-#1012 gate hardcoded its vendor root, so pointed at a case it would have read the real repository rather than answering blindly. This is the plausible weaker check written instead: confirm every pinned path is present under the subtree and call that vendored - 'complete' mistaken for 'correct'. It catches a deleted file and is blind to one edited in place. It MISSES the known-bad input and AGREES with the current gate on the known-good one.
